name: Email Signature
description: An on-brand SUSE email signature, ready to paste into any client.

inputs.label: Headshot
inputs.help: Optional headshot. Displayed as a circle.

inputs.label: Links
inputs.help: Named links shown on one line under your contact details - a booking page, your team portal, LinkedIn. Rows with no title or no address are skipped.

inputs.label: Logo
inputs.help: Select Grey if you think most of your audience prefers dark mode

inputs.label: Name weight
inputs.help: Font weight of your name (100 Thin → 900 Black).

inputs.label: Title weight
inputs.help: Font weight of the job title line (100 Thin → 900 Black).

inputs.label: Email Promo
inputs.help: Optional promo banner below the signature. Scaled to fit within 400×200px, aspect preserved.

tracks.label: On a computer
steps: Open **Export**, set the format to **HTML**, and press **Copy**. The signature goes to your clipboard as formatted text, images and all.
In Gmail, open **Settings** (the cog, top right) and choose **See all settings**.
On the **General** tab, scroll to **Signature** and create one, or select the one you already have.
Click into the signature box and paste (**Ctrl+V**, or **Cmd+V** on a Mac).
Scroll to the bottom and press **Save Changes** - Gmail discards the signature if you leave without it.
tracks.note: Outlook, Apple Mail and Thunderbird take the same paste: copy as HTML, then paste into their signature editor.

tracks.label: On a phone
steps: Tap **Export**, set the format to **HTML**, and tap **Copy**.
Open Gmail in your phone's **browser** (not the Gmail app) and switch it to the desktop site - **aA → Request Desktop Website** on iPhone, **⋮ → Desktop site** on Android.
Go to **Settings → See all settings → General → Signature**, paste into the box, and press **Save Changes**.
tracks.note: The Gmail app's own signature setting is plain text only, so a signature with a logo has to be set this way once. It then applies to mail you send from the app too.
